ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p62/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p62/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p62/r5.claim: The Prophet should patiently receive and convey revelation rather than rush to recite it; God guarantees its collection, preservation, explanation, and elucidation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p62/r5.anchor: The Almighty is revealing it as per His wisdom and expediency.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r3.claim: The pronoun in ‘when We recite it’ refers to the angel who conveys the Qur’an; follow it first with your mind and attention, says Ibn ʿAbbas.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة: فاتبع حلاله واجتنب حرامه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة والضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r4.claim: Another report from Ibn ʿAbbas, and reports from Qatada and al-Dahhak, take following the recitation as obeying its commands and prohibitions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r4.anchor: وقال أيضا هو قتادة والضحاك: فاتبع في الأوامر والنواهي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r5.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya has a nonstandard reading with qaf, ra, and ta open and no hamza or alif in the three occurrences; the author explains its altered morphology.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو العالية: فإذا قرته فاتبع قرته، بفتح القاف والراء والتاء من غير همز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r11.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the revelation is to be listened to or followed in its contents; Qatada specifies that its lawful is followed and its forbidden avoided.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p348/r11.anchor: وعنه أيضا: فإذا يتلى عليك فاتبع ما فيه. وقال قتادة: فاتبع حلاله واجتنب حرامه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p349/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p349/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p349/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains that the Prophet hurried both to memorize and ask about meaning; the command assures preservation and defers questions until recitation ends.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p349/r1.anchor: ثم إن علينا بيانه: إذا أشكل عليك شيء من معانيه، كأنه كان يعجل في الحفظ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p239/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p239/r8.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p239/r8.claim: The surah describes gathering on Judgment Day in gathering bones and sun with moon, and earthly gathering in collecting and reciting the Quran.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p239/r8.anchor: وذكرت نوعين من الجمع، جمعاً في يوم القيامة وجمعاً في الدنيا

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r10.claim: If the address were to humanity generally, the pronouns could refer to a person’s inward knowledge: do not rush to voice it, since God gathers and recites it and one should follow.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r10.anchor: hesab başında Hakk’ın huzûrunda vicdânındakini acele söyleyip de işin içinden çıkacağım diye telaş etme

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r11.claim: The pronoun’s antecedent is not explicit; a universal-human addressee could make it refer to what is within a person, namely conscience.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r11.anchor: Bu âyetteki بِهِۦ zamirlerinin merci‘i zâhir değildir. Hitab mutlak insana olsaydı

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r12.claim: Because the address is specifically to the Prophet and the passage later names the Qur’an, the pronouns first refer to the Qur’an being revealed; an implied antecedent is sufficient, as at 97:1.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r12.anchor: hitab bilhassa Peygamber’e olmak ve sonra da “Kur’an” denilmiş bulunmak itibariyle bu بِهِۦ zamirinin evvelâ

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r13.claim: The exegetes identify the pronouns as referring to the Qur’an.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r13.anchor: Onun için tefsirler bu بِهِۦ zamirlerinin Kur’ân’a râci‘olduğunu beyan etmektedirler.

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r15.claim: The Prophet should listen while revelation arrives rather than hurry to recite; God undertakes gathering and reciting it, then he follows Gabriel’s completed reading.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r15.anchor: sade dinle, acele okumak için dilini oynatma

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r17.claim: Here “Qur’an” is a verbal noun meaning recitation, though it may also mean the recited text.

ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r22.claim: The revelation discussion is integrated with the preceding account of conscience rather than left as a digression, joining the beginning and end of the passage.
ELMALILI:75:1-30#4/r22.anchor: bu âyetleri bu sûrede bir istitrad hâlinde bırakmayarak evvelini âhirine tamamen yapıştırmıştır.

RAZI-FULL:v30p196#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p196#2/r7.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v30p196#2/r7.claim: Al-Qaffāl proposes that the address concerns a person shown his record at resurrection: God reads and gathers his deeds, commands confession, then explains his punishment; this is a strong warning though unsupported by reports.
RAZI-FULL:v30p196#2/r7.anchor: قال القفال : فهذا وجه حسن ليس في العقل ما يدفعه وإن كانت الآثار غير واردة به

RAZI-FULL:v30p198#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#2/r1.claim: Ascribing Gabriel’s recitation to God indicates Gabriel’s great honor; al-Rāzī compares it with the verse that makes obedience to the Messenger obedience to God.
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#2/r1.anchor: جعل قراءة جبريل عليه السلام قراءته ، وهذا يدل على الشرف العظيم لجبريل عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v30p198#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the command as following Gabriel’s recitation once he has read it.
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس : معناه فإذا قرأه جبريل فاتبع قرآنه

RAZI-FULL:v30p198#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#2/r3.claim: Qatāda interprets following the recitation as following its lawful and unlawful contents.

RAZI-FULL:v30p198#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#2/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī prefers that Muhammad listen silently until Gabriel finishes, then recite; the command here concerns listening rather than obeying legal content.
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#2/r4.anchor: لكن يجب أن تسكت حتى يتم جبريل عليه السلام القراءة ، فإذا سكت جبريل فخذ أنت في القراءة ، وهذا الوجه أولى

RAZI-FULL:v30p198#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that after this verse, the Prophet would lower his head and listen when Gabriel came, then recite after Gabriel departed.
RAZI-FULL:v30p198#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس : فكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا نزل عليه جبريل بعد هذه الآية أطرق واستمع فإذا ذهب قرأه

STUDYQURAN:75:16/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r1.claim: The verses tell the Prophet to wait patiently for revelation to continue, paralleling the instruction in 20:114.
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r1.anchor: These verses address the Prophet, encouraging him to wait patiently for the continuation of the revelation

STUDYQURAN:75:16/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r4.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains “follow its recitation” as listening and remaining silent.
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r4.anchor: Then Ibn ʿAbbās said, “So when We recite it, follow its recitation

STUDYQURAN:75:16/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r6.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r6.claim: After Gabriel left, the Prophet listened to Gabriel’s recitation and then recited the Quran just as Gabriel had recited it.
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r6.anchor: after his departure he used to recite it as Gabriel had recited it

STUDYQURAN:75:16/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r8.claim: The passage can admonish Quran students to read and reflect on all its teachings before drawing hasty conclusions.
STUDYQURAN:75:16/r8.anchor: These verses can also be taken as an admonition to those who wish to understand the Quran to first read and reflect upon all of its teachings

TAB-FULL:v23p502/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p502/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p502/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains “when We recite it” as when God reveals it to Muhammad, and “follow its recitation” as listen to it.
TAB-FULL:v23p502/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {فإذا قرأناه} [القيامة: 18] فإذا أنزلناه إليك

TAB-FULL:v23p502/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p502/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p502/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says that once the Qur’an is recited to Muhammad, he should follow what it contains.
TAB-FULL:v23p502/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {فإذا قرأناه فاتبع قرآنه}

TAB-FULL:v23p502/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p502/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p502/r3.claim: Qatāda says to follow the Qur’an’s lawful commands and avoid its prohibitions.

TAB-FULL:v23p502/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p502/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v23p502/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says to follow what the Qur’an contains.
TAB-FULL:v23p502/r4.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {فاتبع قرآنه} [القيامة: 18] يقول

TAB-FULL:v23p502/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p502/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p502/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the command as “act on it.”
TAB-FULL:v23p502/r5.anchor: عن علي، عن ابن عباس، قوله: {فإذا قرأناه فاتبع قرآنه}

TAB-FULL:v23p502/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p502/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p502/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers taking the command as acting on the recited Qur’an: obey its commands and follow what it directs, since qurʾānah means recitation.
TAB-FULL:v23p502/r6.anchor: وأولى هذه الأقوال بالصواب في ذلك قول من قال

TAB-FULL:v1p89#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p89#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p89#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses 'when We recite it' as 'We made it clear' and 'follow its recitation' as 'act according to it.'
TAB-FULL:v1p89#2/r2.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس، في قوله

TAB-FULL:v1p89#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p89#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p89#2/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers Ibn ʿAbbās's derivation of Qur'an from reciting or reading; he understands the report to mean act on what was clarified through recitation.
TAB-FULL:v1p89#2/r3.anchor: والواجب أن يكون تأويله على قول ابن عباس، من التلاوة والقراءة

TAB-FULL:v1p89#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p89#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p89#2/r4.claim: Another Ibn ʿAbbās report says God undertakes to make the Prophet recite without forgetting; when it is recited to him, he should follow its contents.
TAB-FULL:v1p89#2/r4.anchor: عن أبيه، عن عبد الله بن عباس

TAB-FULL:v1p89#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p89#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p89#2/r5.claim: On Qatāda's account, Qur'an is a verbal noun meaning gathering and joining parts together, as in saying a she-camel has not gathered a fetus.
TAB-FULL:v1p89#2/r5.anchor: على قول قتادة، فإن الواجب أن يكون مصدرا، من قول القائل قرأت الشيء إذا جمعته وضممت بعضه إلى بعض

TAB-FULL:v1p94/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p94/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p94/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī cites ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm's poem using Qur'an to mean recitation, supporting Ibn ʿAbbās's derivation from reading.

TAB-FULL:v1p94/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p94/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p94/r2.claim: He answers that Qur'an may name recitation though the text is recited, just as kitāb can name a written object through the act of writing.
TAB-FULL:v1p94/r2.anchor: قيل كما جاز أن يسمى المكتوب كتابا، بمعنى كتاب الكاتب

TAB-FULL:v1p92/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p92/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p92/r3.claim: Qatādah says following its recitation means following what is lawful in it and avoiding what is forbidden.

TAB-FULL:v1p92/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p92/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p92/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes قرآنه to mean God’s clarification through His recitation: once it is explained to the Prophet, he must follow that explanation.
TAB-FULL:v1p92/r4.anchor: صح ما قال ابن عباس في تأويل قوله

TAB-FULL:v1p92/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p92/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p92/r5.claim: Both Ibn ʿAbbās’s explanation and Qatādah’s composition sense are valid Arabic, but each revealed verse bound the Prophet before the Qur’an was compiled.
TAB-FULL:v1p92/r5.anchor: ولكلا القولين أعني قول ابن عباس وقول قتادة، اللذين حكيناهما، وجه صحيح في كلام العرب

TAB-FULL:v1p92/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p92/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p92/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers Ibn ʿAbbās: otherwise the Prophet would not have been bound to follow 96:1 or 74:1 until compilation, contrary to the community’s doctrine; every verse binds whether compiled or not.
TAB-FULL:v1p92/r6.anchor: ولو وجب أن يكون معنى قوله

TABATABAI:75:16-19/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r1.claim: These four verses interrupt the resurrection description with divine etiquette for the Prophet receiving revelation: listen until recitation is complete. Their instruction resembles 20:114.
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r1.anchor: الآيات الأربع في معنى قوله تعالى ولا تعجل بالقرآن من قبل أن يقضي إليك وحيه

TABATABAI:75:16-19/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r6.claim: Once God completes reciting the revelation to the Prophet, he should follow that recitation and then read it.
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r6.anchor: أي فإذا أتممنا قراءته عليك وحيا فاتبع قراءتنا له واقرأ بعد تمامها

TABATABAI:75:16-19/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r7.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r7.claim: Another interpretation takes following the recitation as listening with full attention; the author considers it acceptable.
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r7.anchor: وقيل المراد باتباع قرآنه اتباعه ذهنا بالانصات والتوجه التام إليه وهو معنى لا بأس به

TABATABAI:75:16-19/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r8.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r8.claim: Other readings say to follow its commands and prohibitions or repeat the recitation until fixed in memory; the author calls both remote.
TABATABAI:75:16-19/r8.anchor: وقيل المراد فاتبع في الأوامر والنواهي قرآنه، وقيل المراد اتباع قراءته بالتكرار حتى يرسخ في الذهن وهما معنيان بعيدان

TABATABAI:75:16-21/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r1.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r1.claim: Some say the Prophet moved his tongue during revelation for fear of forgetting and was told to listen until it ended; the pronoun means what had already been recited to him.
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r1.anchor: وقال بعضهم في معنى هذه الآيات إن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كان يحرك لسانه عند الوحي بما ألقي إليه من القرآن مخافة أن ينساه

TABATABAI:75:16-21/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r2.claim: The fear-of-forgetting account does not fit: the verses more plainly prohibit haste and command following God’s completed recitation, while gathering and recitation supports the author’s reading.
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r2.anchor: وفيه أنه لا يلائم سياق الآيات، تلك الملاءمة نظرا إلى ما فيها من النهي عن العجل والأمر باتباع قرآنه تعالى بعد ما قرئ

TABATABAI:75:16-21/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r3.claim: Another interpreter says these verses concern a person reading his record on Judgment Day, not the Qur’an: God gathers the evidence, demands submission, then explains it if denied.
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r3.anchor: وعن بعضهم في معنى هذه الآيات، الذي اختاره أنه لم يرد القرآن

TABATABAI:75:16-21/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r4.claim: The record-reading view fails because an interrupting passage needs no contextual signs before and after it, and its resemblance to 20:114 supports the Qur’anic reading.
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r4.anchor: ويدفعه أن المعترضة لا تحتاج في تمام معناها إلى دلالة مما قبلها وما بعدها عليه

TABATABAI:75:16-21/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r5.claim: A further view connects the verses to Judgment: do not hasten to ask when it will come; God gathers those destined for it, reveals its description, and clarifies it by the trumpet blast.
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r5.anchor: وعن بعضهم أن الآيات الأربع متصلة بما تقدم من حديث يوم القيامة، وخطاب { لا تحرك } للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:75:16-21/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:16-21/r6.claim: The Judgment-day reading is untenable to the author.

TABATABAI:75:36-39/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that revelation weighed on the Prophet, who moved his lips to memorize; God promised to gather and recite it, told him to listen, and promised its explanation; thereafter he listened to Gabriel and recited after he left.
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يعالج من التنزيل شدة، وكان يحرك به

TABATABAI:75:36-39/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r11.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī notes similar reports from Ibn Jubayr and others, but says the fit between this explanation and the verses is obscure.
TABATABAI:75:36-39/r11.anchor: روى ما في معنى صدر الحديث في المجمع عن ابن جبير وفي معناه غير واحد من الروايات، وقد

BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r9.claim: When Gabriel has finished reciting the Quran, the majestic “We” magnifies the command to wait and listen.
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r9.anchor: أي أتممنا قراءته عليك بلسان جبريل وإسناد القراءة إلى نون العظمة

BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r10.claim: The Prophet should begin reciting immediately after Gabriel finishes, without delay.
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r10.anchor: أي فاشرع فيه بعد فراغ جبريل منه لا مهلة

BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains following the recitation as God establishing it in the Prophet’s breast and his acting upon it.
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r11.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما ، فإذا جمعناه وأثبتناه في صدرك فاعمل به

BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r12.speaker: الواسطي
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r12.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī reads gathering the Quran as inward and recitation as outward.
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r12.anchor: وقال الواسطي رحمه الله جمعه في السر وقرآنه في العلانية

BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r15.speaker: أهل التفسير
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r15.claim: Exegetes say the Prophet recited along with Gabriel before he finished, eager to memorize and fearing he would forget; he was told to listen with heart and ear until revelation ended.
BURSEVI:v10p191#2/r15.anchor: قال أهل التفسير كان عليه السلام إذا لقن الوحي نازع جبريل القراءة ولم يصبر

TABRISI:75:17-24/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:17-24/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:75:17-24/r4.claim: The reading is Gabriel's recitation to the Prophet by God's command, and following it means reciting after Gabriel finishes.
TABRISI:75:17-24/r4.anchor: { فإذا قرأناه } أي قرأه جبريل عليك بأمرنا { فاتبع قرآنه } أي قراءته عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:75:17-24/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:17-24/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:75:17-24/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that after this command the Prophet listened with his head bowed and recited once Gabriel had departed.
TABRISI:75:17-24/r5.anchor: فكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد هذا إذا نزل عليه جبريل ع أطرق فإذا ذهب قرأ

TABRISI:75:17-24/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:75:17-24/r6.speaker: قتادة والضحاك
TABRISI:75:17-24/r6.claim: Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk alternatively take following the recitation to mean acting on its rulings of lawful and unlawful things.
TABRISI:75:17-24/r6.anchor: وقيل: { فاتبع قرآنه } أي فاعمل بما فيه من الأحكام والحلال والحرام عن قتادة والضحاك

THALABI:v10p86#2/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p86#2/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p86#2/r13.claim: Following the recitation means following the rulings it contains.
THALABI:v10p86#2/r13.anchor: فإذا قرأناه عليك فاتبع قرآنه أي ما فيه من الأحكام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p498/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p498/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p498/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Gabriel is the one reciting when God recites it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p498/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فإذا قرأه جبريل (¬5)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p498/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p498/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p498/r2.claim: Muqatil says God recites it to the Prophet through Gabriel.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p498/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p498/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p498/r3.claim: One interpretation is to follow what the Qur’an contains as God recites it; Qatada similarly says to follow its lawful and forbidden rulings.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p498/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p498/r4.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p498/r4.claim: Qatada says to follow the Qur’an’s lawful and forbidden rulings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p498/r4.anchor: ونحو هذا قال قتادة: يقول: فاتبع حلاله وحرامه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p498/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p498/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p498/r5.claim: More plausibly, follow its recitation means recite it after Gabriel finishes, since the Prophet was told to stop reading and listen until Gabriel was done.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p498/r5.anchor: وأجود من هذا أن يكون المعنى: فاتبع قرآنه، أي: اقرأه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p498/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p498/r6.speaker: ابن عباس عن سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p498/r6.claim: In Ibn Abbas’s report through Said ibn Jubayr, the Prophet listened silently when Gabriel came, then recited after Gabriel left, as promised.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p498/r6.anchor: وهذا معنى قول ابن عباس في رواية سعيد بن جبير قال: يقول: إنا أنزلناه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p498/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p498/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p498/r7.claim: Another Ibn Abbas report says to listen and be silent when Gabriel comes, then recite after he departs; this follows Gabriel’s recitation by listening.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p498/r7.anchor: وقال (¬5) أيضا: فاتبع قرآنه، واستمع له، وأنصت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p500/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p500/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p500/r4.claim: The same analysis makes the phrase mean “follow our reciting it.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p500/r4.anchor: وكذلك التقدير في قوله: {فاتبع قرآنه}، ومجاز الآية على قول أبي عبيدة:

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:17-28/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:17-28/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:17-28/r2.claim: The Prophet should follow the recitation and not hurry ahead before Gabriel has finished.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:75:17-28/r2.anchor: { فإذا قرأناه فاتبع قرآنه } أي: لا تعجل بالتلاوة إلى أن يقرأ عليك.

QASHANI:75:17-19/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:75:17-19/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:75:17-19/r2.claim: When God recites it, He brings it into being during the servant's annihilation; following its recitation means returning to subsistence, with heart and self appearing in the detailed station.
QASHANI:75:17-19/r2.anchor: حال فنائك فينا { فاتبع قرآنه } بالرجوع إلى مقام البقاء بعد اللفناء

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:16/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:16/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:16/r5.claim: The Prophet was told to remain silent and listen when revelation was recited to him, and he did so.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:16/r5.anchor: vahiy kendisine okunduğunda Hz. Peygamber’in susarak onu dinlemesi emredilmiş, o da böyle yapmıştır (Buhârî, “Tefsîr”, 75; Müslim, “Salât”, 148).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:16/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:16/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:16/r6.claim: Although God attributes recitation to Himself here, other verses say Gabriel brought revelation to the Prophet’s heart; there is no contradiction, since revelation through Gabriel is also God’s recitation and God is the source of the Qur’an.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:75:16/r6.anchor: Allah Teâlâ “biz onu okuduğumuz zaman” buyurarak okuma fiilini kendisine isnat etmiştir; başka âyetlerde onu vahiy meleğinin (Cebrâil) Hz. Peygamber’in kalbine indirdiği bildirilmektedir

BURHAN:v3p319/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p319/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p319/r3.claim: The majestic plural can signal agents acting under God's command: winds drive clouds and angels move them, while Gabriel recites and God gathers the guilty; rain revives earth through ordained causes.
BURHAN:v3p319/r3.anchor: فتسوقه الملائكة بأمره وإحياء الأرض به بواسطة إنزاله

ITQAN:v3p293#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p293#3/r1.speaker: بعض الرافضة
ITQAN:v3p293#3/r1.claim: Some Shiʿites alleged that material had dropped from the Resurrection sūra; al-Qaffal, as quoted by al-Razi, instead read these verses as a frightened person rushing through his record of deeds.
ITQAN:v3p293#3/r1.anchor: حتى زعم بعض الرافضة أنه سقط من السورة شيء وحتى ذهب القفال فيما حكاه الفخر الرازي أنها نزلت في الإنسان المذكور قبل

ITQAN:v3p293#3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p293#3/r2.speaker: القفال
ITQAN:v3p293#3/r2.claim: Al-Qaffal explains the passage as addressing a person shown his record, who stammers and reads hastily from fear; he is told to listen, follow the reading by admitting his deeds, and await their explanation.
ITQAN:v3p293#3/r2.anchor: ذهب القفال فيما حكاه الفخر الرازي أنها نزلت في الإنسان المذكور قبل

ITQAN:v3p293#3/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p293#3/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p293#3/r3.claim: Al-Qaffal’s interpretation conflicts with the sound report that these verses were revealed when the Prophet moved his tongue during revelation.
ITQAN:v3p293#3/r3.anchor: وهذا يخالف ما ثبت في الصحيح أنها نزلت في تحريك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لسانه حالة نزول الوحي عليه

ITQAN:v3p293#3/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p293#3/r4.speaker: الأئمة
ITQAN:v3p293#3/r4.claim: The intervening instruction explains that listening closely to revelation and understanding it take priority over hurried memorization; God guarantees its preservation, after which the Prophet should follow it.
ITQAN:v3p293#3/r4.anchor: وقد ذكر الأئمة لها مناسبات منها أنه تعالى لما ذكر القيامة وكان من شأن من يقصر عن العمل لها حب العاجلة

ITQAN:v2p335#5/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p335#5/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p335#5/r1.claim: “When We recite it” is glossed as “when We explain it.”

ITQAN:v2p335#5/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p335#5/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p335#5/r2.claim: “Follow its recitation” means act according to it.

KHATTABI:v1p39/r6.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p39/r6.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p39/r6.claim: They object that 75:16–19 interrupts the flow from the preceding passage about a person's self-witness to the warning about preferring worldly life, and say each topic should occupy its own section.
KHATTABI:v1p39/r6.anchor: وقد يدخل بين الكلامين ماليس من جنسهما ولا قبيلهما كقوله سبحانه

FARRA:v3p211/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p211/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p211/r2.claim: When Gabriel recites it to Muhammad, he should follow that recitation; قراءة and قرآن are verbal nouns.
FARRA:v3p211/r2.anchor: إذا قرأه عليك جبريل عليه السلام

FARRA:v3p211/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p211/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p211/r3.claim: القراءة and القرآن are verbal nouns, like رجحان and رجوح, معرفة and عرفان, طواف and طوفان.
FARRA:v3p211/r3.anchor: كما تقول: راجح بين الرجحان والرجوح. والمعرفة والعرفان، والطواف والطوفان.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p500#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p500#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p500#4/r1.claim: Here “when We recite it” means “when We collect it.”
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p500#4/r1.anchor: {فإذا قرأناه} أي جمعناه. {فاتبع قرآنه} أي جمعه.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p500#4/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p500#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p500#4/r2.claim: He explains “follow its Qur’an” as “follow its collection.”
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p500#4/r2.anchor: {فإذا قرأناه} أي جمعناه. {فاتبع قرآنه} أي جمعه.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p500#4/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p500#4/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p500#4/r3.claim: Qur’an and qirāʾa are both verbal nouns.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p500#4/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p500#4/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p500#4/r4.claim: Qatāda instead explains the command as following the Qur’an’s lawful teachings and avoiding its prohibitions.

MAJAZ:v1p1#45/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p1#45/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p1#45/r1.claim: Qur'an is the name of God's book alone; Abu ʿUbayda derives it from collecting and joining its suras.
MAJAZ:v1p1#45/r1.anchor: القرآن: اسم كتاب الله خاصة، ولا يسمى به شىء من سائر الكتب غيره، وإنما سمى قرآنا لأنه يجمع السور

MAJAZ:v1p1#45/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p1#45/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p1#45/r2.claim: He reads ‘its Qur'an’ as composition: when God has assembled and joined part of it to the Prophet, he should take, follow, and act on it.
MAJAZ:v1p1#45/r2.anchor: ثم قال: «فإذا قرأناه فاتبع قرآنه» (75/ 18) مجازه: فإذا ألفنا منه شيئا، فضممناه إليك فخذ به، واعمل به

MAJAZ:v1p1#45/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p1#45/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p1#45/r3.claim: Amr ibn Kulthum's line uses taqraʾ janīnan for containing a child in the womb; the idiom ma qaraʾat salyan means a woman never conceived.
MAJAZ:v1p1#45/r3.anchor: وقال عمرو ابن كلثوم في هذا المعنى: ذراعى حرة أدماء بكر ... هجان اللون لم تقرأ جنينا

MAJAZ:v1p1#45/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p1#45/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p1#45/r5.claim: The name Furqan means that the Qur'an separates truth from falsehood and believer from unbeliever.
MAJAZ:v1p1#45/r5.anchor: لأنه يفرق بين الحق والباطل، وبين المسلم والكافر، وخرج تقديره على تقدير: رجل قنعان

MAJAZ:v1p1#45/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p1#45/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p1#45/r6.claim: He relates Furqan's form to qanaʿān, a term for a judgment that satisfies both disputants and makes them accept it.
MAJAZ:v1p1#45/r6.anchor: وخرج تقديره على تقدير: رجل قنعان، والمعنى أنه يرضى الخصمان والمختلفان فى الأمر بحكمه بينهما ويقنعان به.

MAJAZ:v1p17/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p17/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p17/r1.claim: He explains jamʿahu wa-qurʾānahu as composition and fa-idhā qaraʾnāhu as collection, supporting this sense with Amr ibn Kulthum's use of qaraʾa for containing a fetus.
MAJAZ:v1p17/r1.anchor: «إن علينا جمعه وقرآنه» (75/ 17) : أي تأليفه «فإذا قرأناه» (75/ 18) أي إذا جمعناه

MAJAZ:v1p17/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p17/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p17/r2.claim: Amr ibn Kulthum's line and the idiom ma qaraʾat salyan use qaraʾa for enclosing a fetus in the womb or never having conceived.
MAJAZ:v1p17/r2.anchor: هجان اللون لم تقرأ جنينا أي لم تضم فى رحمها، ويقال للتى لم تلد: ما قرأت سلى قط.

MAJAZ:v1p17/r7.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p17/r7.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p17/r7.claim: He restates that Qur'an names the collected book and Furqan names its function of distinguishing truth from falsehood and believers from unbelievers.
MAJAZ:v1p17/r7.anchor: والقرآن: اسم كتاب الله، لا يسمى به غيره من الكتب، وذلك لأنه جمع وضم السور ومجازه من قوله

NAHHAS:v5p83/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p83/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p83/r1.claim: Via Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Ibn Abbas glosses the phrase as: when God sends the revelation down, listen to it.
NAHHAS:v5p83/r1.anchor: روى سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس فإذا أنزلناه فاستمع له

NAHHAS:v5p83/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p83/r2.speaker: قتادة
NAHHAS:v5p83/r2.claim: Qatada explains following the recitation as following the Qur’an’s lawful and forbidden rulings.
NAHHAS:v5p83/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة أي فاتبع حلاله وحرامه

NAHHAS:v5p83/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p83/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p83/r3.claim: Al-Nahhas calls Ibn Abi Talha’s report from Ibn Abbas especially good: God explains the Qur’an, and people should act on what it contains.
NAHHAS:v5p83/r3.anchor: ومن حسن ما قيل فيه ما رواه ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس فإذا قرأناه قال يقول فإذا بيناه فاتبع قرآنه قال يقول فاعمل بما فيه

SAMIN-DURR:75:17/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:17/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
SAMIN-DURR:75:17/r4.claim: A noncanonical قرته is analyzed as قرأته, a second-person past meaning when you intend to recite it, with hamza changed to alif and the alif deleted for ease.
SAMIN-DURR:75:17/r4.anchor: وتوجيهها: أن الأصل: " قرأته " فعلا ماضيا مسندا لضمير المخاطب أي: فإذا أردت قراءته

SAMIN-DURR:75:17/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:75:17/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:75:17/r5.claim: The deletion of alif in قرته is compared with ولو تر ما الصبيان, where ما is extra and the expected form is ترى.
SAMIN-DURR:75:17/r5.anchor: ثم حذف الألف تخفيفا كقولهم: " ولو تر ما الصبيان " أي: ولو ترى الصبيان و " ما " مزيدة

ZAJJAJ:v5p252#2/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p252#2/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p252#2/r6.claim: The Prophet is told not to hurry in reciting until the revelation for its proper time has been recited to him.
ZAJJAJ:v5p252#2/r6.anchor: أي لا تعجل بالتلاوة إلى أن تقرأ عليك ما ينزل في وقته

ASAD-NOTES:75:16/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:75:16/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:75:16/r3.claim: When God recites it, the Prophet should follow its wording attentively.
ASAD-NOTES:75:16/r3.anchor: when We recite it, follow thou its wording

ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r2.claim: The passage also applies to every believer who reads, listens to, or studies the Qur'an, and should be read with 20:114 and its note 101.
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r2.anchor: both have also a wider import inasmuch as they apply to every believer who reads, listens to or studies the Qur'an

ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r3.claim: While 20:114 warns against hasty conclusions from isolated verses, this passage calls for patient study of the whole message and careful attention to every word and phrase.
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r3.anchor: not to draw hasty - and therefore potentially erroneous - conclusions from isolated verses or statements of the Qur'an

ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r4.claim: Readers and listeners should avoid mechanical fluency or delight in beautiful Qur'anic sound without understanding its message.
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n6/r4.anchor: remain satisfied with the mere beautiful sound of the Qur'anic language without understanding

ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n8/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n8/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:75:16#n8/r1.claim: Following the recitation means following the message as expressed in words; God attributes the recitation to Himself because He reveals the Qur'an and enables human understanding.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p213/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p213/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p213/r4.claim: To follow the recitation means to follow it with one's mind and thought—that is, to listen.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p213/r4.anchor: ومعنى: {فَاتَّبِعْ قُرْآنَهُ} أي: اتّبعه بذهنك وفكرك، أي: فاستمع له

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p214/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p214/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p214/r1.claim: The plural attribution both honors God and reflects that Gabriel actually recites and clarifies under God's command; God directs and the angel transmits.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p214/r1.anchor: ذلك أن القارئ هو جبريل، وليس الله

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p214/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p214/r2.speaker: التفسير الكبير
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p214/r2.claim: Al-Tafsīr al-Kabīr says Gabriel's recitation is attributed to God, analogously to calling obedience to the Messenger obedience to God.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p214/r2.anchor: جاء في (التفسير الكبير) في قوله تعالى: {فَإِذَا قَرَأْنَاهُ فاتبع قُرْآنَهُ} "جعل قراءة جبريل عليه السلام قراءته

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p214/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p214/r3.speaker: البحر المحيط
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p214/r3.claim: Al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ identifies the reciter as the angel who conveys God's message.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p214/r3.anchor: وجاء في (البحر المحيط) : "فإذا قرأناه، أي: الملَك المُبلِّغ عنا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p765/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p765/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p765/r3.claim: Qurʾān originally is the verbal noun of قرأ, like غفران and عدوان, and later became the proper name of the revelation sent to the Prophet.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p765/r3.anchor: كلمة " قرآن " هي في الأصل في اللغة مصدر الفعل "قرأ" مثل غفران وعدوان

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p765/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p765/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p765/r4.claim: كتاب derives from writing; revelation may be called a book although sent recited rather than written, since it had already been inscribed in the Preserved Tablet.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p765/r4.anchor: لم يُنزّل مكتوباً وإنما أُنزل مقروءاً ولكنه كان مكتوباً في اللوح المحفوظ

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p765/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p765/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p765/r5.claim: A surah introduced through the Book tends to repeat كتاب more than قرآن, one introduced through the Quran tends to repeat قرآن more, and a surah introducing both uses them at roughly equal rates.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p765/r5.anchor: أما عندما يبدأ بالقرآن يتردد في السورة ذكر كلمة (القرآن) أكثر من (الكتاب

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r4.claim: These verses tell the Prophet to be patient amid his opponents’ pressure and repeated demands, while he waits for revelation to answer them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r4.anchor: These verses urge the Prophet (sws) to be patient on the hast iness and various new

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r5.claim: Only revelation gave the Prophet the guidance needed to carry out his grave duty of publicly warning his people; he depended on his Lord at every step.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r5.anchor: He was like a soldier, fighting at a battle front, who could not move even one step without guidance from his Lord.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r7.claim: They also objected that a Qur’an from God should have been revealed all at once, and used such challenges to obstruct the Prophet’s mission.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r7.anchor: Similarly, they would object that if the Qur’ ān was God’s word

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r8.claim: Revelation strengthened the Prophet’s heart and resolve, renewed his soul, and guided his intellect as he faced his opponents.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r8.anchor: It was through divine revelation that his heart would receive strength, his soul would be rejuvenated, his intellect guided

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r9.claim: The Qur’an and Hadith indicate that during divinely wise pauses in revelation the Prophet looked toward heaven; when Gabriel recited, he was eager to learn and preserve every word.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p72/r9.anchor: Consequently, it is evident both from the Qur’ ān and Ḥad īth

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r3.claim: The Prophet needed revelation for the strategy of his mission as God’s Messenger.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r3.anchor: All the strategy that needed to be adopted by him in the capac ity of

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r4.claim: Revelation alone could meet his spiritual, moral, and intellectual needs.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r4.anchor: His spiritual, moral and intellectual needs could only be fulfille d

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r5.claim: It supplied guidance for circumstances the Prophet faced and those still to come.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r5.anchor: He would receive from it the guidance needed to face existing and future circumstances.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r6.claim: It enabled him to answer the objections and demands his adversaries continually raised.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r6.anchor: It was through it that he was able to answer the objections and demands which his adversaries would keep posing

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r7.claim: His love of knowledge and care to preserve it also contributed to his eagerness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r7.anchor: His great love for knowledge and his sensitivity in preserving it also contributed very much to it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r8.claim: Though the Prophet’s motives were noble, divine wisdom required gradual revelation, so he was repeatedly urged to be patient.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r8.anchor: it was God’s wisdom that the Qur’ ān be revealed gradually

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r9.claim: The Prophet receives a similar exhortation to patience in Sūrah Ṭāhā.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r9.anchor: In S ūrah Ṭāhā (114-115) too he has been similarly urged.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r10.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r10.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r10.claim: Here the Prophet is also assured that God will preserve, collect, arrange, recite, and explain the Qur’an, so he can be content with what is revealed and leave its timing to God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r10.anchor: here he has been subsequently assured of the preservation of the Qur’ ān also.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r11.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r11.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r11.claim: He should accept the portion revealed, avoid anxiety about its preservation, and trust that each task will be completed at its appointed time.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p73/r11.anchor: He was also not to worry about its preservation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p74/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p74/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p74/r5.claim: The Prophet should follow the recital he receives, read and act on it, and call people to it; God determines the pace and arrangement, so he need not heed demands for one-time revelation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p74/r5.anchor: responsibility was to only follow the recital

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r1.speaker: Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r1.claim: Farāhī accepts the exegetes’ view that haste partly reflected fear of losing Qur’anic material, while adding that the Prophet saw himself entrusted with a grave responsibility.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r1.anchor: I do not differ with this view; however, there are some more details

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r2.speaker: Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r2.claim: Farāhī says the Prophet feared accountability for losing even a letter, while also seeking more revelation to guide his people; the assurance addresses both concerns.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p75/r2.anchor: he thought that he was being given a great responsibility

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r3.speaker: Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r3.claim: Farāhī concludes that collection, arrangement, and a recital sequence occurred during the Prophet’s lifetime, since he was told to follow the newly recited text.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r3.anchor: If this promise was to be fulfilled after his death, he would not have been aske d

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r4.speaker: Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r4.claim: He infers that the Prophet communicated the final Qur’anic sequence as recited to him, matching the original sequence in the Guarded Tablet.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r4.anchor: this directive means that the Prophet (sws) must have communicated the final arrangement of the Qur’ ān

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r6.speaker: Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r6.claim: Farāhī says these conclusions follow from the Qur’an and Hadith: the Prophet recited whole sūrahs in sequence, and Companions memorized and followed that arrangement.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r6.anchor: Consequently, the Prophet (sws) would read out whole sūrahs of the Qur’ ān

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r7.speaker: Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r7.claim: He says the Prophet directed Companions to place each revealed verse in its assigned position within a particular sūrah, and they obeyed.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p76/r7.anchor: direct the Companions (rta) to place the revealed verses

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p77/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p77/r3.speaker: Ḥamīd al-Dīn Farāhī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p77/r3.claim: Authentic, agreed-upon reports say that after the Qur’an was fully revealed Gabriel recited it to the Prophet in its true sequence, resolving doubts about its arrangement.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p77/r3.anchor: once the whole of the Qur’ ān had been revealed, Gabriel recited the complete Qur’ ān

NASHR:v1p414/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p414/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
NASHR:v1p414/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr transfers the hamza’s vowel in these Quran forms, including Quran al-fajr, qurʾānan farraqnāhu, and fa-ttabiʿ qurʾānahu.

NASHR:v1p440/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p440/r1.speaker: بعض النحاة
NASHR:v1p440/r1.claim: Some grammarians permit substitution and assimilation of hamza across separate words; Abu Amr reports this from some Arabs.
NASHR:v1p440/r1.anchor: وذكر بعض النحاة الإبدال والإدغام في المنفصل نحو (في أنفسكم وقالوا آمنا) وحكاه أبو عمرو في (الفرخ)

NASHR:v1p440/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p440/r2.speaker: أبو طاهر بن سوار وأبو الفتح بن شيطا
NASHR:v1p440/r2.claim: Abu Tahir ibn Sawwar and Abu al-Fath ibn Shita also allow substitution and assimilation in separate-word hamza.
NASHR:v1p440/r2.anchor: ووافق على جواز ذلك من القراء أبو طاهر بن سوار وأبو الفتح بن شيطا

NASHR:v1p440/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p440/r3.speaker: نحاة الكوفة
NASHR:v1p440/r3.claim: Kufan grammarians allow hamza between hamza and a vowel after any vowelless letter, as after a vowel.
NASHR:v1p440/r3.anchor: وأجاز نحاة الكوفيين أن تقع همزة بين بين بعد كل ساكن كما تقع بعد المتحرك

NASHR:v1p440/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p440/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
NASHR:v1p440/r4.claim: Abu Hayyan says the Kufan allowance for intermediate hamza after any consonant conflicts with Arabic usage.
NASHR:v1p440/r4.anchor: أبو حيان في " الارتشاف "، وقال هذا مخالف لكلام العرب

NASHR:v1p440/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p440/r5.speaker: أبو العلاء الهمداني
NASHR:v1p440/r5.claim: Abu al-Ala al-Hamdani uniquely treats waw and ya after a long vowel like alif, allowing intermediate hamza after any of them.
NASHR:v1p440/r5.anchor: وانفرد أبو العلاء الهمداني من القراء بالموافقة على ذلك فيما وقع الهمز فيه بعد حرف مد

NASHR:v1p440/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p440/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p440/r6.claim: Ibn al-Jazari considers that extension very weak: intermediate hamza is used after alif because transfer and assimilation are impossible there, unlike after waw or ya.
NASHR:v1p440/r6.anchor: فإنهم إنما عدلوا إلى بين بين بعد الألف لأنه لا يمكن معها النقل ولا الإدغام

NASHR:v1p440/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p440/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v1p440/r7.claim: Al-Dani attributes the practice in mawʾilan and al-mawʾuda to Abu Tahir ibn Abi Hashim; it is especially plausible in mawʾilan because of the written form.
NASHR:v1p440/r7.anchor: أن الحافظ أبا عمرو الداني حكى ذلك في (موئلا، والموءودة) وقال: إنه مذهب أبي طاهر بن أبي هاشم

NASHR:v1p440/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p440/r8.speaker: بعض النحاة
NASHR:v1p440/r8.claim: Some grammarians allow deleting hamza after long-vowel waw or ya instead of transferring it, as in tazdari aʿyunukum and adʿu ila.
NASHR:v1p440/r8.anchor: أجاز بعض النحاة الاستغناء عن النقل بعد الياء والواو إذا كانا حرفي مد بحذف الهمزة

NASHR:v1p440/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p440/r9.speaker: القراء
NASHR:v1p440/r9.claim: No Qurʾan reader accepts deleting hamza after long-vowel waw or ya.
NASHR:v1p440/r9.anchor: ولم يوافق على هذا التخفيف أحد من القراء، وأجاز النحاة النقل بعد الساكن الصحيح مطلقا

NASHR:v1p440/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p440/r10.speaker: القراء
NASHR:v1p440/r10.claim: Readers reject unrestricted transfer after a vowelless consonant: they permit it after ordinary consonants, but not after plural mīm.
NASHR:v1p440/r10.anchor: ولم يوافقه القراء على ذلك، فأجازوا في غير ميم الجمع نحو (قد أفلح، وقل إني) لا في نحو (عليكم أنفسكم، ذلكم إصري)

NASHR:v1p440/r11.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p440/r11.speaker: أبو الحسن السخاوي
NASHR:v1p440/r11.claim: Al-Sakhawi says readers in his tradition agree to pronounce the hamza fully in such cases when pausing.
NASHR:v1p440/r11.anchor: فقال الإمام أبو الحسن السخاوي لا خلاف في تحقيق مثل هذا في الوقف عندنا

NASHR:v1p440/r12.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p440/r12.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p440/r12.claim: Ibn al-Jazari endorses the readers’ restriction: moving hamza would change plural mīm’s original ḍamma, so some connect it before hamza to restore that vowel.
NASHR:v1p440/r12.anchor: وهذا هو الصحيح الذي قرأناه به، وعليه العمل، وإنما لم يجز النقل في ذلك ; لأن ميم الجمع أصلها الضم

QIRAAT-ER:75:18:6#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:75:18:6#1/r1.speaker: hmz
QIRAAT-ER:75:18:6#1/r1.claim: The hamza-lightened quranahu removes the medial glottal catch while retaining the recitational noun and possessive suffix.
QIRAAT-ER:75:18:6#1/r1.anchor: hmz, mutawatir: Canonical hamza-lightened reading removes the medial glottal catch while retaining the recitational noun

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p334#4/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p334#4/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p334#4/r2.claim: Qatāda explains following its recitation as following the Qurʾān's lawful and forbidden rulings.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p334#4/r2.anchor: ﴿ فإذا قرأناه فاتبع قرآنه ﴾ يقول فاتبع حلاله وحرامه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#3/r1.claim: When Gabriel has completed reciting the revelation to the Prophet on God’s behalf, the Prophet must follow its recitation; the attribution to God is figurative.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#3/r1.anchor: بلسان جبريل عليه السلام المبلغ عنافا فالأسناد مجازي

ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#3/r2.claim: The emphatic “We” heightens the command to wait and follow the recitation rather than compete with it.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#3/r2.anchor: مع اختيار نونالعظمة مبالغة في إيجاب التأتي فاتبع قرآنه فكن مقفيا له لا مباريا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#3/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#3/r3.claim: A sound report from Ibn Abbas explains the command as following the reading mentally, listening, and remaining silent.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#3/r3.anchor: وقيل أي فإذا قرأناه فاتبع بذهنك وفكر كقرآنه فاستمع وأنصت وصح هذا من رواية الشيخين وغيرهما عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#3/r4.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#3/r4.claim: Qatada and others take following the Qur’an to mean obeying its commands and prohibitions.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#3/r4.anchor: وعنه أيضا وعن قتادة والضحاك أي فاتبع في الأمر والنواهي قرآنه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#3/r5.speaker: الضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#3/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak is also reported to interpret following the Qur’an as obeying its commands and prohibitions.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#3/r5.anchor: وعنه أيضا وعن قتادة والضحاك أي فاتبع في الأمر والنواهي قرآنه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#3/r6.claim: A further view understands the command as repeatedly reviewing the recitation until it settles firmly in memory.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p142#3/r6.anchor: وقيل اتبع قرآنه بالدرس على معنى كرره حتى يرسخ في ذهنك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r1.claim: God will gather the Quran in the Prophet's breast and enable its recitation; when Gabriel recites it, the Prophet should listen and follow, and God will explain it through his tongue.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r1.anchor: قال علينا أن نجمعه في صدرك، وقرآنه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas's account says the Prophet would bow his head when Gabriel came, then recite after he left; another transmission says he moved his lips for fear the revelation might escape.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r2.anchor: فكان إذا أتاه جبريل عليه السلام أطرق فإذا ذهب قرأه كما وعده الله عز وجل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r3.claim: The transmission through Ibn Abbas explains the gathering as placing the Quran in the Prophet's breast and its quran as his reciting it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p284#2/r3.anchor: عن موسى بن أبي عائشة بهذا الإسناد وقال: كان يحرك شفتيه إذا نزل عليه، يخشى أن ينفلت منه

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r1.claim: The recitation is delivered through Gabriel to the Prophet.

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r2.claim: The Prophet should follow Gabriel's reading and repeat it until it is firmly established in his mind.
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r2.anchor: قراءته وتكرر فيه حتى يرسخ في ذهنك

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r5.claim: The passage reinforces the rebuke against haste: haste is blameworthy even in the most important matter and foundation of religion, and therefore all the more elsewhere; it may also recall an event during revelation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r5.anchor: وهو اعتراض بما يؤكد التوبيخ على حب العجلة

BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r6.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r6.claim: Alternatively, the speech addresses the person receiving his record: he stumbles in fear as he hurries to read it, so God promises to gather and read his deeds; he should acknowledge or reflect on the reading, then God explains it through requital.
BAYDAWI-FULL:75:18-19/r6.anchor: وقيل الخطاب مع الإنسان المذكور والمعنى أنه يؤتى كتابه فيتلجلج لسانه من سرعة قراءته خوفا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p250/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p250/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p250/r1.claim: When Gabriel recites, the Prophet should listen intently, attend with his mind, repeat the passage until fluent, and practice it until it becomes a character that leads to good.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p250/r1.anchor: أي بغاية جهدك بإلقاء سمعك وإحضار ذهنك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p250/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p250/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p250/r2.claim: The pronoun may refer to the Qur’an, meaning Gabriel’s recitation of it, or to Gabriel himself, meaning follow his reading without addressing him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p250/r2.anchor: فالضمير يجوز أن يكون للقرآن أي قراءة جبريل عليه السلام له

BIQAI-FULL:v8p250/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p250/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v8p250/r5.claim: Through Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Ibn ʿAbbās reports that revelation strained the Prophet, who moved his lips; God revealed these instructions, after which he listened silently to Gabriel and recited the passage when Gabriel left. No grading is stated.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p250/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال : ( كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يعالج

DURR-FULL:v8p347/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p347/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p347/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet moved his tongue and lips under revelation’s strain, fearing he would forget; the verses promise collection and recitation, attentive following, and clarification, after which he listened and recited when Gabriel left.
DURR-FULL:v8p347/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يعالج من التنزيل شدة وكان يحرك به لسانه وشفتيه مخافة أن يتلفت منه

DURR-FULL:v8p347/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p347/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p347/r5.claim: A second report says the Prophet hurried to recite each revelation to memorize it and did not know a surah’s end until Bismillah descended.
DURR-FULL:v8p347/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا نزل عليه القرآن تعجل بقراءته ليحفظه

DURR-FULL:v8p347/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p347/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p347/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet persisted in reciting from fear of forgetting; God undertook to gather and recite it so he would not forget, commanded him to follow it, and to explain its lawful and unlawful rulings.
DURR-FULL:v8p347/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يفتر عن القرآن مخافة أن ينساه فقال الله

DURR-FULL:v8p347/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p347/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p347/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says “when We recite it” means “when We make it clear,” and following its recitation means acting upon it.
DURR-FULL:v8p347/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس {فإذا قرأناه} قال: بيناه {فاتبع قرآنه} يقول: اعمل به

DURR-FULL:v8p348/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p348/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p348/r3.claim: Qatadah interprets following the recitation as following what is lawful and avoiding what is forbidden.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3387#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3387#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3387#3/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains fa-idhā qaraʾnāhu as “when We made it clear.”
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3387#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس : فاذا قراناه قال : بيناه

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3387#3/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3387#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3387#3/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains following its recitation as acting upon it.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3387#3/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس : فاذا قراناه قال : بيناه فاتبع قرانه يقول : اعمل به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p349/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p349/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p349/r2.claim: The reading is Gabriel’s reading on God’s behalf; attributing it to the divine pronoun is a clear case of figurative attribution.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p349/r2.anchor: أي إذا قرأه جبريل عنا ، فأسندت القراءة إلى ضمير الجلالة على طريقة المجاز العقلي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p349/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p349/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p349/r3.claim: Following the recitation means listening attentively to it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p349/r3.anchor: ومعنى { فاتبع قرآنه } ، أي أنصت إلى قراءتنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p349/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p349/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p349/r4.claim: The pronoun in قرأناه refers to the same Quran as the pronoun in لا تحرك به, treating Quran as the thing read.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p349/r4.anchor: فضمير { قرأناه } راجع إلى ما رجع إليه ضمير الغائب في { لا تحرك به }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p349/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p349/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p349/r5.claim: The passage’s insertion resembles 19:64 and the prayer command in 2:238, which appears amid the marriage rulings of al-Baqara.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p349/r5.anchor: فيكون وقوع هذه الآية في هذه السورة مثل وقوع { وما نتنزل إلا بأمر ربك } في سورة مريم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r1.claim: Because the Quran is Arabic, Arabic linguistic knowledge is the route to its meanings; those without native Arabic intuition risk misunderstanding.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r1.anchor: ذلك يقع الغلط وسوء الفهم ، لمن ليس بعربي بالسليقة ، ونعني بقواعد العربية مجموع علوم اللسان العربي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r2.claim: Arabic language sciences include lexicon, morphology, syntax, rhetoric of meanings, and rhetoric of exposition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r2.anchor: ونعني بقواعد العربية مجموع علوم اللسان العربي ، وهي : متن اللغة ، والتصريف ، والنحو

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r3.claim: Exegetes must also know established Arab usage in speeches, poetry, and eloquent constructions; native speakers' intuitions can illuminate meanings unclear to later Arabs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r3.anchor: ومن وراء ذلك استعمال العرب المتبع من أساليبهم في خطبهم وأشعارهم وتراكيب بلغائهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the exegete must preserve the Quran's fine structure, complete eloquence, and unblemished challenge when interpreting it; language neglect compromises that work.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r4.anchor: قال في الكشاف : ومن حق مفسر كتاب الله الباهر ، وكلامه المعجز أن يتعاهد في مذاهبه بقاء النظم على حسنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r5.claim: The sciences of maʿani and bayan are especially important to tafsir because they reveal Quranic rhetorical features, detailed meanings, and the grounds of its inimitability; they were once called dalail al-iʿjaz.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r5.anchor: ولعلمي البيان والمعاني مزيد اختصاص بعلم التفسير لأنهما وسيلة لإظهار خصائص البلاغة القرآنية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says expertise in law, kalam, reports, preaching, grammar, or lexicon alone does not enable someone to uncover tafsir's truths; the interpreter must excel in maʿani and bayan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r6.anchor: قال في الكشاف : علم التفسير الذي لا يتم لتعاطيه وإجالة النظر فيه كل ذي علم ، فالفقيه وإن برز على الأقران

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r8.speaker: السكاكي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r8.claim: Al-Sakkaki says grasping the full intent of God's speech requires both maʿani and bayan, and warns against interpreting without them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r8.anchor: وقال السكاكي في مقدمة القسم الثالث من كتاب المفتاح : وفيما ذكرنا ما ينبه على أن الواقف على تمام مراد الحكيم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r9.speaker: السيد الجرجاني
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r9.claim: Al-Jurjani agrees that Quranic stylistic features exceed those of other speech, so anyone lacking natural eloquence needs maʿani and bayan to recognize them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r9.anchor: قال السيد الجرجاني في شرحه : ولا شك أن خواص نظم القرآن أكثر من غيرها فلابد لمن أراد الوقوف عليها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r10.claim: Ibn Ashur says al-Sakkaki aptly called God al-Hakim: wise speech carries elevated aims and meanings that rhetorical practice is needed to uncover.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r10.anchor: وقد أصاب السكاكي بذكر الحكيم المحز ، أي أصاب المحز إذ خص بالذكر هذا الاسم من بين الأسماء الحسنى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r11.claim: Sakkaki's word yuna bbih suggests the need should be obvious yet is often neglected; his warning of woe deters, since untrained interpreters usually err and even rare success does not excuse their undertaking.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r11.anchor: وفي قوله ينبه إشارة إلى أن من حقه أن يكون معلوما ولكنه قد يغفل عنه ، وقوله فالويل كل الويل تنفير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r12.claim: Full intent may mean the entirety of God's intended Quranic meaning, an aspirational goal for interpreters, or the specific meanings marked by rhetorical signs and constrained by context.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r12.anchor: وقوله تمام مراد الحكيم ، أي المقصود هو معرفة جميع مراد الله من قرآنه ، وذلك إما ليكثر الطلب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r13.claim: The possible meanings are effectively inexhaustible and spur effort; people differ in how much they uncover according to their acuity and knowledge.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r13.anchor: والكل مظنة عدم التناهي وباعث للناظر على بذل غاية الجهد في معرفته ، والناس متفاوتون في هذا الاطلاع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r14.speaker: أبو الوليد ابن رشد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r14.claim: Ibn Rushd calls ignorant the claim that Arabic is unnecessary and says no religious or Islamic matter is sound without Arabic, citing 26:195; he says a speaker acting from corrupt intent should repent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r14.anchor: وقال أبو الوليد ابن رشد ، في جوابه له عمن قال : إنه لا يحتاج إلى لسان العرب ما نصه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r15.speaker: أبو الوليد ابن رشد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r15.claim: Ibn Rushd says that when denial of Arabic's necessity stems from corrupt religious intent, the imam disciplines the speaker as he sees fit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p18#2/r15.anchor: إلا أن يرى أنه قال ذلك لخبث في دينه فيؤدبه الإمام على قوله ذلك بحسب ما يرى فقد قال عظيما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p421#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p421#3/r1.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p421#3/r1.claim: The Prophet is to recite after Gabriel finishes reciting.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p421#3/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون يعني اقرأ إذا فرغ جبريل من قراءته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p421#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p421#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p421#3/r2.claim: Following its recitation means acting according to it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p421#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس فاتبع قرآنه أي اعمل به

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p421#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p421#3/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p421#3/r3.claim: Following it means observing what it permits and forbids.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r1.claim: God teaches the Prophet to listen rather than race the angel in receiving revelation, promising to collect it in his heart, enable its recitation, and explain it; these are its three stages.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r1.anchor: هذا تعليم من الله عز وجل لرسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في كيفية تلقيه الوحي من الملك، فإنه كان يبادر إلى أخذه، ويسابق الملك في قراءته

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r5.claim: “When We recite it” means when the angel recites it to the Prophet on God’s behalf.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r5.anchor: فإذا قرأناه} أي: إذا تلاه عليك الملك عن الله عز وجل،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r6.claim: The Prophet is to listen to the angel and then recite the Quran as the angel taught it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r6.anchor: فاتبع قرآنه} أي: فاستمع له، ثم اقرأه كما أقرأك،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that revelation caused the Prophet strain and he moved his lips; God told him to listen while Gabriel recited, promised to gather the Quran in his chest, and afterward the Prophet recited it as taught.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يعالج من التنزيل شدة، فكان يحرك شفتيه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r9.speaker: البخاري ومسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r9.claim: Bukhari and Muslim transmit the report by multiple routes; Bukhari’s wording says the Prophet lowered his head when Gabriel came, then recited after Gabriel left as God had promised.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p278#2/r9.anchor: وقد رواه البخاري ومسلم، من غير وجه، عن موسى بن أبي عائشة، به (2) ولفظ البخاري: فكان إذا أتاه جبريل أطرق، فإذا ذهب قرأه

JISHUMI:v10p7183/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7183/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7183/r15.claim: Following, emulating, and imitating are near-synonyms; following means the second thing conforms to the first, opposite to differing from it.
JISHUMI:v10p7183/r15.anchor: والاتباع والاقتداء والاحتذاء نظائر، والاتباع: موافقة الثاني للأول

JISHUMI:v10p7186/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7186/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v10p7186/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains following its recitation as reciting it oneself after hearing it.
JISHUMI:v10p7186/r1.anchor: أي: اتبع قرآنه بقراءتك، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v10p7186/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7186/r2.speaker: قتادة، والضحاك
JISHUMI:v10p7186/r2.claim: Qatādah and al-Ḍaḥḥāk interpret following its recitation as acting on the Qurʾān's rulings.
JISHUMI:v10p7186/r2.anchor: وقيل: فاعمل بما فيه من الأحكام، عن قتادة، والضحاك

JISHUMI:v10p7186/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7186/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7186/r3.claim: Another explanation is to act on the Qurʾān and convey it to the Prophet's community.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p662#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p662#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p662#2/r6.claim: God calls Gabriel's recitation His own; the Prophet should follow Gabriel rather than prompt him during recitation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p662#2/r6.anchor: قرءانه } فكن مقفيا له فيه ولا تراسله

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says that once God has clarified the Quran, the Prophet should act on it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r6.anchor: أحدها : فإذا بيناه فاعمل بما فيه , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r7.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas takes the command to mean: once it is revealed, listen to its recitation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r7.anchor: الثاني : فإذا أنزلناه فاستمع قرآنه , وهذا مروي عن ابن عباس أيضا .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r8.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r8.claim: Qatada says that once it is recited to the Prophet, he should follow its laws and rulings.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p155#2/r8.anchor: الثالث : فإذا تلي عليك فاتبع شرائعه وأحكامه , قاله قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p21/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p21/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p21/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas derives Quran from qara'a meaning to make clear, citing the command to follow its recitation as an instruction to act on what God explains.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p21/r7.anchor: وهو قول عبد الله بن عباس ، مصدر من قولك قرأت أي بينت ، استشهادا بقوله تعالى : ^ ( فإذا قرأناه فاتبع قرآنه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#9/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#9/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#9/r1.claim: “When We recite it” means when Gabriel recites it to the Prophet; Gabriel's recitation is attributed to God.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#9/r1.anchor: أي قرأه عليك جبريل فجعل قراءة جبريل قراءته

NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#9/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#9/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p300#9/r2.claim: The Prophet should follow Gabriel's recitation as it is read to him.

QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r2.claim: The Muslim and Bukhari account says the Prophet listened to Gabriel recite, then recited as taught; Ibn Abbas and Saʿid demonstrate the lip movement.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r2.anchor: عن ابن جبير عن ابن عباس قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يعالج من التنزيل شدة

QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r3.claim: God gathers the revelation in the Prophet’s breast and recites it to him; he is to listen and follow its recitation.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r3.anchor: قال جمعه في صدرك ثم تقرؤه

QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r7.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r7.claim: Al-Farraʾ treats qirāʾa and Qurʾān as verbal nouns; Qurʾānah here means recitation to the Prophet.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r7.anchor: والقراءة والقرآن في قول الفراء مصدران

QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r8.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r8.claim: Qatada interprets following the recitation as following the Qur’an’s laws and rulings.
QURTUBI-FULL:75:16-21/r8.anchor: قال قتادة: «فاتبع قرآنه» أي فاتبع شرائعه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān links the passage to the contrast between a denier absorbed in sinful desires and someone who preserves, studies, and presents God’s signs in hope of acceptance; opposites reveal each other.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r4.anchor: وقال أبو حيان يظهر أن المناسبة بين هذه الآية وما قبلها أنه سبحانه لما ذكر منكر القيامة والبعث معرضا عن آيات الله تعالى ومعجزاته وأنه قاصر شهواته على الفجور

ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r6.speaker: القفال
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r6.claim: Al-Qaffāl reads the command as addressing the human being when shown his record: fear makes him stumble and rush through it, so he is told not to move his tongue hastily.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r6.anchor: وقال القفال قوله تعالى لا تحرك الخ خطاب للإنسان المذكور في قوله تعالى ينبؤ الإنسان وذلك حال إنبائه بقبائح أفعاله يعرض عليه كتابه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r7.speaker: القفال
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r7.claim: On al-Qaffāl’s view, God promises to assemble the person’s deeds, read them to him, have him acknowledge or consider the record, and then explain its consequences and punishment; this is a severe threat of a detailed account.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r7.anchor: فإنه يجب علينا بحكم الوعد أو بحكم الحكمة أن نجمع أعمالك وأن نقرأها عليك فإذا قرأناه عليك فاتبع قراءته بالأقرار

ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r8.speaker: البلخي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r8.claim: Al-Balkhī and his followers prefer al-Qaffāl’s reading: the pronouns refer to the record implied by 75:13 and the sentence is circumstantial, introduced by an implied saying, at the presentation of the book.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r8.anchor: ومن هنا اختاره البلخي ومن تبعه لكنه مخالف للصحيح المأثور الذي عليه الجمهور

ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r9.speaker: القفال
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r9.claim: Al-Qaffāl's reading that the person receiving his record is addressed differs from the authentic majority transmission that the address is to the Prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p143/r9.anchor: وقال القفال قوله تعالى لا تحرك الخ خطاب للإنسان المذكور في قوله تعالى ينبؤ الإنسان

ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r1.claim: In the alternative reading, this is a prohibition on asking about the Day’s timing, framed as not opening one’s mouth to rush for its knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r1.anchor: لا تحرك به أي بطلب توقيته لسانك وهو نهي عن السؤال

ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r2.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r2.claim: The Imam suggests the Prophet’s haste may have been explicitly permitted until the prohibition came; al-Ālūsī finds this account problematic.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r2.anchor: وقال الإمام لعل ذلك الاستعجال إن كان مأذونا فيه عليه الصلاة والسلام إلى وقت النهي

ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r4.claim: An alternative reads the direct address as the Prophet, a generic addressee, or any suitable listener; the pronoun refers to the Day of Resurrection, and the sentence interrupts the threat to intensify its terror.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r4.anchor: أنه يكون الخطاب في لا تحرك الخ لسيد المخاطبين حقيقة أو من باب إياك أعني واسمعي أو لكل من يصلح له وضمير به ونظائره ليوم القيامة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r5.claim: On that alternative, the passage means not to hasten to learn the Day’s timing: God will gather creation, reveal its conditions in the Qurʾān, and manifest it at the blast; demanding its date is contrary to wisdom.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r5.anchor: إن علينا جمعه ما يكون فيه من الجمع وقرآنه ما يتضمن شرح أحواله وأهواله من القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī says this alternative has serious difficulties and is not the best explanation; he points instead to Zamakhsharī’s account as fitting the Qurʾān’s eloquence and subtle indications.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p144/r6.anchor: وفيه ما فيه وما كنت أذكره لو لا هذا التنبيه واللائق بجزالة التنزيل ولطيف إشاراته ما أشار إليه ذو اليد الطولي جار الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404#2/r1.claim: The recitation to be followed is the angel messenger's recitation on God's behalf.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says to follow the recitation with one's mind and thought, meaning to listen attentively.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404#2/r2.anchor: أن يريد بذهنك وفكرك، أي فاستمع قراءته وقاله ابن عباس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة والضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404#2/r3.claim: They say the instruction is to follow the Qur'an's commands and prohibitions.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404#2/r3.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد فاتبع في الأوامر والنواهي، قاله ابن عباس أيضا وقتادة والضحاك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404#2/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404#2/r4.claim: Abu al-Aliya reads قرته and فاتبع قرته without hamza, and without the alif in the third form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p404#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو العالية: «قرته» ، «فإذا قرته فاتبع قرته» بفتح القاف والراء والتاء
